about: Advisories the weekly watch doesn't raise, each with why. npm entries are by package and cover only packages outside the web vault and the extension; cargo entries are by advisory and package version. Review the reasons whenever what we ship changes.

npm.node-forge: The command-line tool uses it only to read other password managers' exports when importing (Keeper, LastPass, DuckDuckGo). Its advisory for 1.4.0 and earlier (GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv) is about checking RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures, which it never does there. Take 1.4.1 or later at the next dependency update, once it's two weeks old.
npm.multer: Only the command-line tool's local API (`passbundle serve`, on localhost unless its `--hostname` says otherwise) uses it, for attachment uploads. Its advisories before 2.5.0 let something that can already reach that port stop the server (denial of service); nothing else. Take 2.5.0 or later once it's two weeks old.
npm.inquirer: The command-line tool's prompts in the person's own terminal (text, password, and lists; never the editor prompt). Its advisories are its editor prompt's (external-editor, tmp).
npm.external-editor: Comes with inquirer, for its editor prompt, which the command-line tool never shows.
npm.tmp: Comes with inquirer's editor prompt, which the command-line tool never shows, and build tooling; its advisory is about file names a caller chooses.
npm.ws: Node's WebSocket, under SignalR and jsdom. The browser apps use the browser's own WebSocket, and the command-line tool loads neither for it: it has no live notifications, and uses jsdom only to read import files.
npm.vite: Build tooling (through vite-tsconfig-paths); none of it runs in the web vault or the extension.
npm.immutable: Comes with vite, build tooling only.
npm.nanoid: Comes with vite and postcss, build tooling only.
npm.picomatch: Comes with vite, build tooling only.
npm.postcss: Comes with vite, build tooling only: it reads only our own CSS.
npm.source-map-js: Comes with postcss, build tooling only.

cargo.RUSTSEC-2023-0071 rsa 0.9.10: No fixed version exists. The server signs its login tokens with it (jsonwebtoken, also openidconnect), as upstream Vaultwarden does; the timing leak needs very many precisely timed private-key operations. The desktop agent only encrypts with a public key, which the attack doesn't affect. Revisit when rsa has a fix, or move jsonwebtoken to its aws-lc-rs backend.
cargo.RUSTSEC-2026-0349 rustls 0.21.12: From Rocket 0.5.1, for serving TLS itself; this advisory is about TLS clients or features Rocket doesn't use, and our deployments terminate TLS at a reverse proxy. Revisit when Rocket moves to a newer rustls.
